variants.headline: Company lays off many workers
variants.sub: Many workers have been laid off by a company in the colony.
variants.body:
A company has laid off many workers in {colony}. The scale is described as large, but a specific number is not supplied here. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish the loss of jobs from an invented cause, severance arrangement or account of what will happen to those affected.

A layoff is about people whose work matters to their lives. Labour should begin there, with solidarity rather than an abstract admiration for flexibility. The report does not tell every household's story, and we should not invent one to make the case that workers deserve decent treatment when employment ends.

We hold {target} to account critically. A large loss of jobs is not a minor adjustment in the lives of workers, and its stewardship deserves a more demanding standard than a convenient abstraction. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
